description: A0 baseline: raw 13 features, 5-fold LightGBM, no FE
notes: HYPOTHESIS: none - this is the reference point. PURPOSE: open the OOF<->LB paired series (playbook s4) and establish the champion-to-beat. GATE: n/a. MECHANISM: raw features, LightGBM routes categoricals natively; no supervised transform anywhere.

description: A0s: A0 at model_seed=1337 - seed-noise floor
notes: HYPOTHESIS: none. PURPOSE: measure the seed-noise floor (playbook s6/s10). |OOF(A0s)-OOF(A0)| and the paired bootstrap of their difference set the resolution below which no probe result is a result. GATE: n/a.

description: A0s7: A0 at model_seed=7 - seed-noise floor
notes: PURPOSE: third/fourth point for the seed-noise floor SD. GATE: n/a.

description: A0s2024: A0 at model_seed=2024 - seed-noise floor
notes: PURPOSE: third/fourth point for the seed-noise floor SD. GATE: n/a.

description: B1: censoring indicators for the income=30000 and commute=5.0 floors
engineered: inc_at_floor,com_at_floor
notes: HYPOTHESIS: both numerics are censored at their floor (9.2% and 21.6% of rows sit exactly there), so each floor value mixes two populations - the genuinely-low and the clipped. MECHANISM: a tree can only separate them with an exact-equality split it has no reason to find; an explicit indicator hands it the partition. This is what makes the income logit curve non-monotone at its bottom decile. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: B2: log(Annual_Income_USD) alongside the raw column
engineered: log_income
notes: HYPOTHESIS: none, expected null. MECHANISM: trees are invariant to monotone transforms of a split variable, so log-income can only help via the histogram binning (equal-width bins in log space resolve the dense low end more finely). Run as a deliberate negative control: if this moves, the binning is doing more work than assumed. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: B3: drop the 4 flat-in-logit columns (Gender, Number_of_Cars_Owned, both Charging_Stations_*)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: these 4 are generator noise - per-value logits are flat to within +/-0.1 and single-feature AUCs are 0.505-0.524. MECHANISM: if noise, removing them is variance reduction (fewer spurious splits, less colsample dilution of the real drivers), not a wash. If OOF DROPS, they carry conditional signal and the flat marginal was hiding it. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: B4: per-value target encoding of Annual_Income_USD (13,214 values), fold-fit
notes: HYPOTHESIS: TE was S6E8's single largest feature win. MECHANISM: it hands the tree a column already monotone in log-odds, so one split captures what otherwise needs many. BUT S6E8's data was a value->target lookup table and this one is smooth-monotone in income, so the prior here is weaker than it was there. SUPERVISED transform - fit on the train fold only, training rows encoded via an inner 5-fold. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: B5: per-value target encoding of the 3 numerics (income, commute, age)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: B4 extended. MECHANISM: Age is non-monotone (rate dips at 29-34, peaks at 51-56) and commute is non-monotone with a clipped floor, so both are shapes a TE recovers directly and a tree must spend depth on. If B5 > B4, the win is coming from the NON-monotone columns, which is the mechanism worth knowing. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: B6: monotone-increasing constraint on Annual_Income_USD
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the income->target relation is monotone increasing everywhere except the clipped bottom decile, which is an artifact rather than signal. MECHANISM: the constraint is a regularizer - it forbids the tree from fitting the non-monotonic wiggle, which should be noise. If it LOSES, the bottom-decile non-monotonicity is real signal and B1's clip indicator is the better tool for it. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: B7: more capacity, slower learning rate (255 leaves, lr 0.02, min_child 100)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: A0's parameters were never tuned - they were a first guess, and it early-stopped at 213-381 iterations, which is fast enough to suggest it saturates before exhausting the data. MECHANISM: 668k rows can support far more capacity than 63 leaves; a lower LR with more regularization should reach a finer per-feature shape. This sizes how much of the 0.0048 gap to the public top is plain tuning. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C1: hierarchical TE - rare values back off to their income neighborhood, not the global prior
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the biggest single win available on top of B5. MECHANISM: income carries a REAL monotone trend underneath the lookup (Spearman(value, per-value rate)=0.68). B5 shrinks a value seen 3 times toward the global prior 0.1746, discarding that trend entirely; a value at income 160k seen 3 times should shrink toward the ~0.34 rate of its neighbourhood instead. With 13,214 values over 668k rows the tail of rare values is where most of the encoding error lives, so fixing the backoff target should be worth more than fixing the smoothing strength. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C2: te_smooth 20 -> 5 (trust rare values more)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: B5's smoothing was an untested default. MECHANISM: smoothing trades lookup fidelity against noise in rare values. If the lookup is strong and the per-value counts are large (mean ~50 rows/value), less smoothing should recover more of it. Paired with C3 this brackets the optimum rather than testing one arbitrary point. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C3: te_smooth 20 -> 100 (trust rare values less)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the other bracket of C2. MECHANISM: if C3 beats B5 the encoding is currently overfitting rare values; if C2 beats B5 it is over-shrinking them. Both losing means 20 was already near-optimal and the smoothing axis is closed. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C4: add log1p(train-fold value count) alongside each TE column
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the model cannot currently tell a TE built from 1,000 rows from one built from 3. MECHANISM: the count is the encoding's own reliability, so handing it over lets the tree discount unreliable TE values in exactly the region where the encoding is worst. This is the cheap alternative to fixing the backoff (C1) and the two may be redundant - if both win, test them together before shipping both. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C5: capacity 63 -> 15 leaves
notes: HYPOTHESIS: LOWER capacity should win, which is the opposite of the usual reflex. MECHANISM: two measurements point the same way - the GLM probe found all 28 pairwise interactions worth +0.000033, and B7 found that RAISING capacity to 255 leaves cost -0.000894. With a genuinely additive generator, extra leaves can only fit interactions that do not exist, which is pure variance. Now that TE has moved the per-value signal into the feature itself, the tree needs even less depth to reach it. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C6: capacity 63 -> 7 leaves
notes: HYPOTHESIS: C5 pushed further, to bracket the capacity optimum rather than testing one point. MECHANISM: as C5. If C6 > C5 > B5 the trend is monotone toward an additive model and the next probe is stumps (num_leaves=2), which is a GAM. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: C7: extend TE to all 7 numeric columns
notes: HYPOTHESIS: expected null, run as a control. MECHANISM: the 4 added columns have 4-20 distinct values each, and LightGBM's 255-bin histogram already resolves them exactly - there is no lookup structure a TE can reveal that a split cannot already reach. If this WINS, the mechanism is not resolution but something else (e.g. TE giving the tree a pre-ordered axis), and that would change what C5/C6 mean. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: D1: te_smooth 5 -> 2
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the smoothing bracket is monotone and has not turned over yet - 100 gave -0.000667, 20 is the B5 baseline, 5 gave +0.000487. MECHANISM: at ~50 rows per income value the per-value rate is already well estimated, so shrinkage is mostly discarding signal rather than controlling noise. Push until it turns over; the turnover point is the answer, a single tested point is not. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: D2: C2 + hierarchical neighborhood backoff (C1 stacked on C2)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: C1 gave +0.000428 on top of B5 (smooth=20). MECHANISM: backoff target and smoothing STRENGTH are two ways to fix the same problem - an unreliable rare-value estimate. C2 already fixed part of it by shrinking less. If D2's delta over C2 is much smaller than C1's over B5, they are redundant and only one should ship; if it holds up, they address different parts of the rare-value tail and both belong. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: D3: C2 + value-count feature (C4 stacked on C2)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: C4 gave +0.000456 on top of B5. MECHANISM: as D2 - the count is a third route to the same rare-value problem, and it is the most general of the three because it lets the tree decide how to discount rather than fixing the discount in advance. Same redundancy test. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: D4: C2 + 7 leaves (C6 stacked on C2)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: capacity is monotone downward - 255 leaves -0.000894, 63 baseline, 15 +0.000212, 7 +0.000268. MECHANISM: the generator is additive (all 28 pairwise interactions worth +0.000033), so leaves beyond what the per-feature shapes need can only fit interactions that do not exist. Unlike the encoder fixes this axis is ORTHOGONAL to the TE, so it should stack cleanly rather than redundantly. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: D5: C2 + 3 leaves (one step from stumps)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: D4 pushed one step further, to find where the capacity bracket turns over. MECHANISM: num_leaves=3 permits a depth-2 interaction at most; num_leaves=2 would be stumps, i.e. a literal GAM with no interactions at all. If D5 >= D4 the additive reading is confirmed to its limit and stumps are the next probe. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: E1: D4 + neighborhood backoff (the two winning axes combined)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: this should stack close to additively, unlike C1/C2/C4 which did not. MECHANISM: the encoder axis (what a rare value shrinks toward) and the capacity axis (how many interactions the tree may fit) address different error sources - encoding bias vs interaction variance - so unlike the three encoder fixes they are not three routes to one problem. If the combined delta is materially less than +0.000177+0.000212, that reading is wrong. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: E2: D4 with te_smooth 5 -> 2
notes: HYPOTHESIS: D1 found +0.000123 for this step at 63 leaves. MECHANISM: at lower capacity the tree can no longer partially correct a noisy encoding by splitting around it, so the optimal smoothing may be HIGHER, not lower, than it was at 63 leaves. This probe tests whether the smoothing optimum moved when capacity changed - if it did, the two axes are not separable and E1's premise is weakened. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: E3: average the training-row TE over 4 independent inner splits
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the headline variance-reduction probe. MECHANISM: a training row's TE is built from 4/5 of the fold, and WHICH 4/5 is an arbitrary draw that injects noise into the feature the model leans on hardest. Averaging over 4 draws cancels it without weakening the leakage guarantee - every draw still excludes the row's own label. If the competition is now a variance problem rather than a signal problem, this is where it shows. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: E4: XGBoost leg on the D4 representation
notes: POOL MEMBER, not an ablation. MECHANISM: same features, different split-finding and regularization, so its errors should point somewhere slightly different from LightGBM's. Judged by ADD/SWAP contribution to the stack, never by solo score - S6E8 measured solo deltas spanning 0.033 AUC while the corresponding stack contributions spanned 0.00006. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: E4: XGBoost leg on the E1 representation
notes: POOL MEMBER, judged by ADD/SWAP contribution to the stack, never by solo score - S6E8 measured solo deltas spanning 0.033 AUC against stack contributions spanning 0.00006. MECHANISM: same features, different split-finding and regularization, so its errors should point somewhere slightly different from LightGBM's. Both are leaf-wise here (grow_policy=lossguide, max_leaves=7), so expect HIGH correlation with E1 - this leg's value, if any, is in the residual disagreement a fitted stack can subtract, not in diversity of inductive bias.

description: E5: CatBoost leg on the E1 representation (symmetric trees)
notes: POOL MEMBER, judged by ADD/SWAP contribution to the stack, never by solo score - S6E8 measured solo deltas spanning 0.033 AUC against stack contributions spanning 0.00006. MECHANISM: CatBoost's oblivious trees apply the SAME split at every node of a level - a strong structural regularizer and a genuinely different inductive bias from leaf-wise LightGBM, which is the kind of difference a fitted stack can use to subtract correlated error. This is the most promising pool member for that reason. 3000 iterations at lr 0.08 for CPU wall-clock; depth is CatBoost's default 6, so unlike E1/E4 it is NOT capacity-matched - a confound accepted because this is a pool member, not a twin.

description: E5: CatBoost leg on the D4 representation (symmetric trees)
notes: POOL MEMBER, not an ablation. MECHANISM: CatBoost's oblivious/symmetric trees apply the SAME split at every node of a level, which is a strong structural regularizer and a genuinely different inductive bias from leaf-wise LightGBM - exactly the kind of difference that can subtract correlated error in a fitted stack. Iterations reduced to 4000 for CPU wall-clock; it is a pool member so this is not a twin violation. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: F1: income ALSO as a native LightGBM categorical, alongside its TE
engineered: cat_Annual_Income_USD
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the cheap test of the 'tokens' idea the public frontier is using (top notebooks: 'EV Adoption Tokens: XGBoost + TinyTokenTransformer', '94.6+ Transformer and GBDT Ensemble'). MECHANISM: TE compresses each of 13,214 income values to ONE number, its target rate. That is a rank-1 summary of the value's identity. LightGBM's categorical split instead sorts levels by accumulated gradient/hessian at each node and cuts the sorted order, so the grouping can DIFFER between nodes - a strictly richer use of value identity than a single fixed scalar. If value identity carries anything beyond its marginal rate, this is where it shows on the cheap. GATE: +0.0001 OOF.

description: F2: E1 with 3-seed bagging inside each fold
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the second test of the 'this is now a variance problem' reframe, after E3 failed it. MECHANISM: averaging 3 models trained on the SAME rows cancels fitting randomness - row/feature subsampling draws and split tie-breaking - without touching the split. Playbook s6: this is the seed manipulation that paid in S6E7, as opposed to re-running at a new OUTER split seed, which measurably bought nothing because test predictions are already averaged over 5 fold-models. The measured seed-noise floor here is 0.000038, which bounds how much seed-to-seed SCORE variation there is, but not directly how much averaging PREDICTIONS can buy. GATE: +0.0001 OOF.

description: logit stack, 6 legs, C=0.1
notes: Phase 2 first stack: 6 legs. Third test of the variance reframe after E3 and F2 both null.

description: G1: token-embedding MLP - value identity as a learned low-rank vector
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the regularized form of the token idea, and the first genuinely NEW representation since the TE. MECHANISM: target encoding compresses each of 13,214 income values to ONE scalar, its marginal target rate - a rank-1 summary. An embedding gives each value 16 numbers, so it can carry more about the value than its marginal rate, while weight decay + dropout + low rank stop it memorizing the way F1's free-form categorical split did (-0.000999, best_iter 1000 -> 182). TE features are kept alongside, so this tests whether identity carries anything BEYOND its rate. Judged as a POOL MEMBER: its solo score matters less than whether it decorrelates from the 0.9922-0.9995 pack, which is what the 6-leg stack showed we lack. GATE: solo within ~0.001 of E1 AND OOF-logit correlation vs E1 below 0.99.

description: G2: G1 retuned - lower LR, less embedding capacity
notes: HYPOTHESIS: G1's representation is right but its TRAINING was broken, so its solo weakness is not evidence about the idea. MECHANISM: G1 peaked at epoch 3 of a 25-epoch OneCycle schedule, i.e. while the LR was still ramping UP - it found its best point during warmup and then degraded as the LR rose past useful. That is a schedule bug, not a capacity verdict. G2 lowers max_lr 1e-3 -> 3e-4 and matches the schedule length to 15 epochs so the peak is not an artifact of warmup, and cuts per-value capacity (emb_dim 16 -> 8, min_count 5 -> 20) to fight the same memorization that killed F1. GATE: this is a POOL MEMBER - it needs solo >= the 0.945402 pool floor to be able to contribute at all (playbook s6: a leg below the floor contributes nothing however decorrelated), while KEEPING G1s max-corr near 0.95 against a pack whose internal median is 0.9973.

description: H1: E1 + TE on QUANTILE-BIN keys of the 3 numerics (100 bins, smoothing 500)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the one concrete untested idea the public frontier offers (README, 'Reading the leaderboard's shape') - TE over quantile-BINNED keys with very heavy smoothing (their TARGET_SMOOTHING=500) rather than our raw per-value keys at te_smooth=5. MECHANISM: this is NOT a contradiction of C3 (raw-value keys at smoothing 100 lost 0.000667). A bin holds thousands of rows against a raw value's ~50, so smoothing 500 shrinks a well-estimated bin rate only slightly; what the column carries is the DENOISED LOCAL TREND, whereas te_ carries the per-value lookup. E1 already computes exactly this quantity - the neighborhood bin rate - but uses it only as a BACKOFF TARGET for rare values and never exposes it to the learner. At 7 leaves the tree has little capacity to reconstruct a smooth trend from the noisy per-value column itself, so handing it the smoothed version is cheap. If this is null, the trend is already fully carried by raw income + te_income and the frontier's binning is a different route to the same place. GATE: +0.0001 OOF over E1 (0.945642).

description: H2: E1 + TE on 5 PAIRED keys (20 bins per numeric component, smoothing 1500)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the second half of the frontier's encoder recipe (PAIR_TARGET_SMOOTHING=1500). Prior is NEGATIVE on two counts - the GLM probe found all 28 pairwise interactions worth +0.000033, and the joint-key residual test found no cross-feature lookup (8 of 9 keys at 0.85-0.95, the income x concern outlier at 1.074 being the largest of nine tests, i.e. selection). MECHANISM, and why it is worth running anyway: those two measurements were made against models with capacity to fit interactions. E1 deliberately has num_leaves=7, chosen BECAUSE the generator is additive - so E1 can barely represent a 2-way interaction even where one exists. A paired-key TE hands specific interactions over as pre-computed columns, which is a far cheaper way to buy them than raising capacity (B7: 255 leaves cost 0.000894). This is therefore a joint test of 'are there interactions' and 'did the capacity cut throw any away'. Pairs chosen as the strongest drivers, not by search, so no selection effect. If null, the additive reading is confirmed a third time, by a third mechanism, and the encoder axis is closed for good. GATE: +0.0001 OOF over E1 (0.945642).

description: H3: E1 + a SINGLE paired key (income x concern), to isolate H2s mechanism
notes: HYPOTHESIS: H2 lost 0.000521 and its best_iter collapsed from ~1000 to ~330 - the F1 signature. Two competing explanations. (a) DISPLACEMENT: income x concern alone reaches solo AUC 0.877 (measured in the leak check), i.e. it is nearly a complete model in one column; the tree eats it greedily, early-stops before refining the additive per-feature shapes E1 spends 1000 rounds building, and so trades fine structure for a coarse 100-cell lookup. (b) ACCUMULATION: five extra correlated columns each carry encoding noise and dilute colsample. GATE, pre-registered as a DISCRIMINATOR not a shipping gate: if one pair loses of order the same 0.0005 as five, the cause is (a) displacement by the dominant key; if it loses roughly a fifth, the cause is (b). Shipping gate is still +0.0001 over E1 (0.945642) and this is not expected to clear it.

notes: Phase 3 slot 3: playbook s6 'find the elbow and stop' - 3 legs vs 6.

notes: Phase 3 slot 3: playbook s6 'test both, assume neither'. The FIXED half has never been computed in this repo.

notes: Phase 3 slot 3: playbook s6 'find the elbow and stop' - 3 legs vs 6.

description: I1: E1 with ALL feature interactions forbidden (a boosted GAM)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: >= E1. MECHANISM: the generator is measured additive three independent ways, so every interaction the 7-leaf tree fits is noise it is paying variance for. Forbidding them is a pure variance cut with no bias cost -- IF the additivity finding is right. If I1 loses materially, real interactions survive at 7 leaves and the additive story has a crack, which is worth as much as the win. GATE: +0.0001 OOF solo (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor), then ADD and SWAP at constant pool size - only the second is a shipping decision.

description: I2: I1 with capacity restored to 63 leaves
notes: HYPOTHESIS: I2 > I1, recovering something like B7's -0.000894. MECHANISM: capacity was cut 63 -> 7 because capacity BOUGHT INTERACTIONS and interactions are absent. With interactions forbidden by construction, num_leaves buys only per-feature shape resolution, which is exactly the lever this data rewards (B4's per-value TE was +0.003017). If the capacity and additivity axes do NOT interact this way, the mechanism attributed to B7 is wrong. GATE: +0.0001 OOF solo (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor), then ADD and SWAP at constant pool size - only the second is a shipping decision.

description: G1r: reproduce G1 (embedding MLP) with cfg now archived, control for the bagging test
notes: HYPOTHESIS: reconstructs G1 (OOF 0.943401) closely enough to serve as the strict-twin baseline for the in-fold seed-bagging test, since G1's own cfg is unrecoverable (the harness gap this run exists to close: run_local.py printed the resolved cfg but never wrote it to preds_dir). MECHANISM: G1's override is inferred from G2's notes (epochs 25->15, so G1=25) and E1's TE recipe (te_cols/te_smooth/te_backoff), which G1's own notes say were kept alongside the embedding. RESULT: exact match -- OOF 0.943401 and all 5 fold AUCs identical to the original G1 row bit-for-bit. Reconstruction confirmed exact, not approximate.

description: G1rB: G1 with 3-seed in-fold bagging (F2's treatment, applied to the embedding leg)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: Phase 3's variance-averaging mechanism is right, so bagging closes most of G1's OOF->LB gap by giving the OOF the same fold-averaging the test predictions already get. MECHANISM: an OOF row is scored by ONE fold-model; a test row already averages FIVE (one per fold). For a net that early-stops at epoch 3-4, that is a large variance cut the OOF never sees. Seed-bagging 3 models per fold approximates that averaging inside the OOF itself. CONTROL: the same treatment bought E1 only +0.000034 (F2), since a 1000-round GBDT is already low-variance -- so a jump near G1's own +0.00105 LB miss (not E1's +0.000034) is the signature that vindicates embeddings and convicts Phase 2b of a biased ruler; a jump near E1's control says the miss is not variance. GATE: OOF jump >= 0.0005 (half the miss). RESULT: OOF 0.943401 -> 0.944074, +0.000673 -- 20x E1's control, 64% of G1's own LB miss. GATE CLEARED: this is variance, not a genuine weakness of the representation. Phase 2b's rejection of G1 used a biased ruler; embeddings deserve a re-test as a bagged pool member before being written off.

description: J1: E1 with learning_rate 0.05 -> 0.02 (shrinkage axis, never probed)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: Phase 3b showed capacity wins by buying per-feature SHAPE RESOLUTION (7 leaves + ~1000 rounds beats 63 leaves), not interaction fitting. Every capacity probe so far changed num_leaves; the step size itself (learning_rate=0.05, a Phase-0-era default) was never probed. If shape resolution is the real lever, slower shrinkage should resolve the same univariate curves more finely -- pushing the SAME confirmed axis one step further, not a new untested mechanism. MECHANISM: smaller lr trades step size for round count at more total granularity; n_estimators=12000 cap and early_stopping_rounds=100 unchanged so early stopping decides the real depth. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor), and best_iter should sit clear of both 0 and the 12000 cap or the result is not trustworthy.

description: K1: E1 with min_child_samples 20 -> 5 (same shape-resolution axis, a different untuned knob)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: min_child_samples=20 is also a Phase-0-era default, never probed once the champion moved to 7-leaf trees. If per-feature shape resolution is the lever (Phase 3b), a looser leaf-occupancy floor lets 7-leaf splits track the per-feature curve more tightly wherever there is enough data (668k rows / 7 leaves is nowhere near the 20-row floor's true purpose of protecting rare categories, most of which the TE already handles). MECHANISM: same axis as J1 (extract more shape resolution from the confirmed-good capacity regime) via a different knob, to see whether J1's null was specific to shrinkage or the whole axis is exhausted. GATE: +0.0001 OOF (interim, ~2.6x the 0.000038 seed-noise floor).

description: L1: E1 with drop_noise=True (SHAP follow-up: do the 4 flat-in-GLM columns carry real OOF signal at champion capacity?)
notes: HYPOTHESIS: a SHAP dependence check on E1 fold-0 (this session, no slot) found Charging_Stations_Near_Home has a non-monotonic swing (-0.073 at 3-7, +0.094 at 13) despite being flagged flat-in-logit noise by the Phase-0 GLM screen -- the exact class of blind spot (linear screen misses non-monotonic per-value effect) that hid income's lookup table. But unlike income (13,214 values), this column has only 15 distinct values, well within what a 7-leaf tree run for ~1000 rounds can carve natively -- so the SHAP structure may already be fully exploited rather than a missed lever. MECHANISM: B3 tested dropping these 4 columns on the UNENGINEERED A0 baseline and found ~0 (0.941648 vs 0.941656); this repeats the test at champion capacity/TE, where a low-cardinality per-value effect would show up as an OOF loss if real and as a null if the SHAP structure is fitting noise the model doesn't actually need. GATE: a loss >= 0.0001 says these columns carry real signal SHAP correctly surfaced past the GLM's blind spot; a null repeats B3's verdict at higher capacity and closes the question.

description: M1: Explainable Boosting Machine (GA2M), additive-only, on E1's TE recipe -- new architecture test
notes: HYPOTHESIS: the generator is confirmed additive in log-odds 4 independent ways. An EBM with interactions=0 is a pure additive GAM by construction, purpose-built for exactly this structure. If additive is the complete story, EBM should be competitive with E1's LightGBM on the same TE features. MECHANISM: cyclic gradient boosting of per-feature step functions, a genuinely different fitting procedure from LightGBM's greedy tree sequence. CatBoost native categorical handling uses ORDERED target statistics -- permutation-based, leak-resistant, structurally different from our static fold-fit TE and from LightGBMs free-form categorical split (F1, -0.000999). MECHANISM TESTED: if manual TE already extracts everything extractable (Phase 1c residual-variance-ratio 0.846, near floor), handing raw identity to a second encoder is redundant -- null or negative. CONCLUSION: a differently-regularized (ordered-TS) categorical mechanism does not escape the displacement failure mode -- it is a property of handing ANY tree learner the raw high-cardinality identity as a single categorical split target, not specific to LightGBMs unregularized split search. Confirms the encoder axis is closed a further way. No slot spent: negative OOF delta.

description: O2: EBM with interactions=8 (auto-detected pairwise terms) vs M1 interactions=0
notes: HYPOTHESIS: M1 (interactions=0) matched E1 within 0.0002/fold, the strongest additivity confirmation yet. Untested: whether EBMs OWN principled interaction search (FAST algorithm, picks highest-marginal-gain pairs) finds anything worth having, vs GLMs brute-force all-28 (+0.000033) or a hand-picked paired-key TE (H2/H3, both negative via displacement). MECHANISM: if generator is truly additive, auto-selected interactions should carry near-zero real gain, so spending model capacity/rounds on them should be neutral-to-negative rather than helpful. RESULT: OOF 0.945015 vs M1 0.945550, Delta -0.000535 -- NEGATIVE, worse than the pure-additive EBM. CONCLUSION: this is the fifth independent confirmation of additivity (after GLM pairwise terms, the additive_only tree constraint, joint-key residual ratios, M1 matching E1 fold-for-fold, and now an automatic interaction-selection algorithm actively hurting when allowed to add terms). The mechanism likely mirrors the capacity/interaction-forbidding finding (Phase 3b): rounds/capacity spent fitting the 8 selected interactions come out of the additive per-feature shape-resolution budget that is the actual lever here, so even genuinely-selected interactions cost more in displaced shape-fitting than they return. Wall-clock cost was much higher too: ~1892s vs M1s 163s, since FAST interaction search happens per fold. No slot spent: negative OOF delta.
